Name: Farmer's End - Escalating Combat and Dungeon Difficulty
Author: acharles1
Description:
[center][size=4][b]Farmer’s End[/b][/size][/center]

[center][size=2]Every expedition starts quietly.[/size][/center]
[center][size=2]A few monsters.[/size][/center]
[center][size=2]A few fights.[/size][/center]
[center][size=2]A few more floors.[/size][/center]
[center][size=2]Then the pressure starts to build.[/size][/center]
[center][size=2]
The farther you push, the harder the expedition pushes back.
And if you keep going long enough...
you may eventually reach Farmer’s End..[/size][/center]

[b]What is Farmer’s End?[/b]
[size=2][b]Farmer’s End[/b] is an expedition-based combat pressure system for the Mines, Skull Cavern, Volcano, and compatible modded progression areas.[/size]
[size=2]Threat is based on how far you progress during a single expedition, not the absolute floor you start on.[/size]
[size=2]Start deep? Things are still calm.[/size]
[size=2]Keep pushing? That’s when the expedition begins to escalate.[/size]


[b]Not Just Stronger Monsters[/b]
[size=2]Farmer’s End does [b]not[/b] make every monster permanently stronger.[/size]
[size=2]The challenge increases because [b]you keep pushing the same expedition[/b].[/size]
[size=2]A fresh run starts calm.[/size]
[size=2]Keep advancing, and the pressure builds through:[/size]
[list]
[*][size=2]more monsters[/size][/*]
[*][size=2]wider awareness and aggro[/size][/*]
[*][size=2]stronger pursuit[/size][/*]
[*][size=2]increased damage at higher threat[/size][/*]
[*][size=2]Breach reinforcements[/size][/*]
[*][size=2]MONSTER AMBUSH![/size][/*]
[*][size=2]and eventually a [b]Farmer’s End[/b] Leaders[/size][/*]
[/list][size=2]The goal is not to turn every enemy into a damage sponge.
The difficulty comes from how far you push the expedition.[/size]


[b]Threat Stages[/b]
[size=2][b]Calm - [/b]Normal monster population and normal awareness.[/size]

[size=2][b]Stirring - [/b]More monsters begin appearing and nearby creatures start reacting sooner.[/size]

[size=2][b]Alert - [/b]Monster pressure increases and enemies notice you from farther away.[/size]

[size=2][b]Hunted - [/b]You are now actively being hunted. Monster numbers rise sharply, enemies focus on you from much greater distances, and monsters also deals 15% more damage[/size]

[size=2][b]Insane - [/b]The expedition reaches maximum pressure. Monster density is at its highest reaching 25% more damage, stronger reinforcements, and a [b]Farmer’s End[/b] Leader can emerge.[/size]


[b]Farmer’s End Leaders[/b]
[size=2]At maximum threat, existing monsters can be promoted into [b]Farmer’s End Leaders[/b][/size]
[size=2]They become:[/size]
[size=2]• larger[/size]
[size=2]• tougher[/size]
[size=2]• harder to knock back[/size]
[size=2]• around 90% more health[/size]
[size=2]• around 35% more damage[/size]
[size=2]• slightly faster[/size]
[size=2]• permanently aware of the farmer[/size]
[size=2]• persistent in their pursuit[/size]
[size=2]• marked by a pulsing red glow[/size]

[size=2]Once Farmer’s End appears, it begins coming for you.[/size]


[b][size=3]MONSTER AMBUSH![/size][/b]
[size=2]Sometimes monsters can end up stranded in unreachable parts of a map. (even in vanilla)[/size]
[size=2]Farmer’s End turns that problem into part of the experience.[/size]
[size=2]If normal ground monsters become genuinely embedded or unreachable, the system can recover them and bring the entire confirmed group back into the fight at once. MONSTER AMBUSH![/size]


[b][size=3]Rewards[/size][/b]
[size=2]Higher threat comes with modest extra rewards.
Defeating all Farmer’s End Leaders grants one additional area-appropriate reward.[/size]


[b][size=3]Combat Overhaul Compatibility[/size][/b][size=2]
Farmer’s End is designed to work alongside most combat overhaul mods.
It does not replace Stardew Valley’s combat system.
Instead, it adds pressure on top of it through:
• expedition threat
• monster population
• awareness and aggro
• Hunted/Insane damage pressure
• Breach reinforcements
• Leader promotion
• bonus rewards
So another mod can change how combat works, while Farmer’s End changes how strongly the expedition responds to you.[/size]


[b][size=3]Why I Made Farmer’s End[/size][/b]
[size=2]I wanted a combat system that still felt like Stardew Valley.[/size]
[size=2]I didn’t want every monster to suddenly become a giant health sponge, and I didn’t want combat difficulty to come from simply multiplying stats.[/size]
[size=2]I wanted the Mines to start familiar and slowly become more dangerous the farther I pushed.[/size]
[size=2]I wanted progression to feel earned, but not so fast that every run became disposable.[/size]
[size=2]Most of all, I wanted mining to feel like an expedition worth diving into again and again.[/size]
[size=2]A run should begin calmly.[/size]
[size=2]Then build.[/size]
[size=2]Then become dangerous.[/size]
[size=2]And eventually reach the point where you have to decide:[/size]
[size=2]Do I leave now... or push one more floor?[/size]
[size=2]That is what Farmer’s End is built around.[/size]

[size=2]In Short[/size]

[size=2]The farther you push, the harder the expedition pushes back.[/size]
[size=2]And if you keep going long enough...[/size]
[size=2]you may eventually reach Farmer’s End.[/size]


[left][size=2][b]📦 Requirements[/b][/size][/left]
[left][size=2]·       [b]Stardew Valley 1.6+[/b][/size][/left]
[left][size=2]·       [b]SMAPI 4.0+[/b][/size][/left]
[left][size=2]·       [b]Generic Mod Config Menu[/b] — Optional[/size][/left]
